problem: Prior Spatial Question Answering (SQA) agents (Meta-Memory, ReMEmbR, Embodied-RAG) rely on closed-source models like GPT-4o for planning and verification. When swapped for comparably sized open-source models, accuracy collapses, especially on global route-constrained queries. Existing SQA benchmarks are also single-pass, mostly indoor/campus tours.
motivation: Real service robots cannot depend on online closed-source models because of network instability, latency and cost, so onboard open-source SQA is needed. The authors argue the gap comes from the lack of an algorithmic primitive matching the data structure, not from weak open-source reasoning: a trajectory is temporally ordered, so two anchor landmarks define a contiguous interval that makes the search one-dimensional.
key_idea: Binary Tracking: recursively halve the trajectory segment interval between two anchor landmarks, descending into the half with stronger semantic evidence and verifying only at the leaf, combined with a multi-view caption memory.
insight: Replacing agent-driven graph reasoning with a structured primitive that exploits temporal order recovers global-query accuracy (62.2%, versus 32.6% for open-source baselines) using only 7B/32B open models. The ablation shows w/o BT drops global from 62.2 to 52.2 and w/o multi-view memory drops it to 48.9 (removing both: 42.2), so both components matter. Failure analysis shows the agent often does not invoke BT (only 49 of 120 global queries do), so tool selection is the main remaining bottleneck.
method: Multi-view memory: each 1.5 s segment (2x2 grid of 4 frames) is captioned three times by Qwen2.5-VL-7B with full/center/detail prompts. Captions are embedded with mxbai-embed-large-v1 and stored as separate Milvus entries, and retrieval ranks across views jointly.

Binary Tracking: finds anchor segment indices by nearest pose to the anchor coordinates, then repeatedly splits the interval at the midpoint. It scores each half with evid = alpha*mean + beta*max of semantic similarity over top-k, keeps the better half until length <= k_leaf=16, then runs the VLM verifier on top-k of the leaf. Cost is O(log n) retrievals plus one verifier call.
Agent loop: Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct-AWQ runs a thought-action loop (step budget 4) over tools SSR, SRR, BT (PATH), legacy MI and FINAL.
Anchor-aware verification pool: the verifier pool is half top-K/2 semantic matches and half the segments closest to the anchor pose.
Lock-on-Y rerank: detects a secondary anchor Y via regex or location nouns, verifies Y candidates, re-sorts Z candidates by distance to Y, and serves as fallback when the step budget runs out.
New benchmark: multi-trip outdoor quadruped (Unitree Go2) dataset with 8 day/night round trips, 383,800 frames, 360 queries, dual robot/human viewpoints, and blurred faces and plates.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct-AWQ planning agent + Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct captioner/verifier + mxbai-embed-large-v1 encoder (all frozen open-source)
setting.model_size: 32B agent (4-bit AWQ), 7B VLM; a 7B-only agent variant fits in about 20GB VRAM
setting.observation: egocentric RGB video (4 frames per 1.5 s segment as 2x2 grid) + 2D robot poses from odometry/SLAM
setting.action_space: Not navigation control: outputs a 2D metric coordinate as the answer (tool actions SSR/SRR/BT/FINAL)
setting.simulator: none (offline recorded trajectories; SpaceLocQA and a real-robot dataset)
setting.privileged: Given trajectory poses for the whole route (memory of pose-tagged frames); anchor coordinates come from the query parser; no other GT

results: BinTrack reaches 67.4% overall on SpaceLocQA (74.4/65.6/62.2 basic/local/global) with only open-source models. This beats the reproduced open-source baselines (ReMEmbR 50.1, Meta-Memory 44.6), matches Meta-Memory's GPT-4o global score of 62.2 and exceeds its GPT-4o overall of 63.9. Latency is 59 s/query versus 111.6 s (Meta-Memory) and 120.3 s (ReMEmbR), a 1.89x/2.04x speedup. On the new benchmark it scores 45.3% versus 18.0% (ReMEmbR) and 15.6% (Meta-Memory).
limitations: Memory is built per trajectory, and naive cross-trajectory retrieval gave no gain.
Captioning requires offline processing of newly visited routes (hours), preventing fully online deployment.
The agent often skips Binary Tracking (only 49 of 120 global queries invoke it), and the 7B verifier misses small objects and Korean signage; the 7B agent loses 12.5 points on global queries.
